notes: Several notable violations: (1) Architectural Rule 1 broken — the Router directly calls both taskService.getById() and userService.getById() inside the POST /comments handler to enrich the comment.added event, constituting a cross-service call mediated by the router rather than the event bus. CommentService also publishes 'comment.added' with empty taskTitle/authorName before the router re-publishes an enriched version, resulting in duplicate event emissions — a significant design flaw. (2) CommentService publishes 'comment.added' internally with blank fields AND the router publishes it again enriched, so NotificationService receives two events per comment creation. (3) The CommentAddedPayload type does not include 'assigneeId', but the notification service casts to 'any' to access it — a type safety violation and a smell indicating the type contract is insufficient. (4) The router acts as an orchestrator beyond pure HTTP handling by reading from two services to enrich events, violating Rule 3 ('all HTTP handling in API Router only' — the router goes beyond HTTP handling into business logic). (5) Status transition allows only one step forward (newIndex === oldIndex + 1), which correctly enforces forward-only but disallows jumping from todo directly to done — this is arguably correct per spec but worth noting. (6) No input validation (missing required fields, invalid UUIDs, etc.) beyond try/catch. (7) GET /tasks without projectId returns 404 rather than all tasks or a proper error. (8) DELETE /projects members uses body on a DELETE request which is fragile. (9) Error responses always return 400 regardless of error type (not found should be 404). (10) All services are in separate files as required. (11) No external npm dependencies. (12) EventBus, types, and interfaces are well-structured. (13) Demo script is functional and exercises main flows. Overall the architecture is partially correct but the comment enrichment approach fundamentally breaks the event bus isolation rule.
